title: Opportunistic Burst Segmentation and Runbook (PRD sketch)
content:
Draft: Opportunistic Burst Segmentation & Tenant Recovery Runbook (PRD sketch)

Context and motivation
- We need a middle ground between hard reserved capacity and fully opportunistic preemptible burst. Customers want predictable baseline throughput but occasional headroom for traffic spikes without long procurement cycles.
- Existing approaches (soft reserve, burst credits) jump between either per-tenant credits or global pools; both have tradeoffs for fairness and recovery time. This doc proposes segmented opportunistic lanes with tenant-level recovery budgets and an operator-friendly runbook for graceful reclamation.

Goals
- Allow short-duration bursts (~5s-3m) that exceed reserved baseline while limiting cross-tenant impact.
- Ensure predictable recovery behavior after bursts so steady-state SLAs aren't violated.
- Make policies expressible via API (per-tenant) and enforceable via scheduler/runtime.
- Provide clear operator steps for debugging and manual remediation.

Key concepts and primitives
- Burst Segments: discrete lanes enumerated by priority and isolation level (e.g., lane-A: high-priority low-isolation, lane-B: balanced, lane-C: opportunistic preemptible).
- Recovery Budget: per-tenant token that drains on burst usage and refills over time (configurable half-life).
- Graceful Reclaim Window (GRW): period after segment allocation where low-priority requests may be drained with warnings (streaming flush hooks).
- Fallback Chains: ordered list of fallback models/variants to route to when reclaim occurs (e.g., gpt-small -> gpt-medium -> safety-response).

API / config surface (proposal)
- tenantCapacity { baseline_rps: int, reserved_gpus: int }
- burstPolicy { segment: string, max_concurrency: int, recovery_budget_initial: float, refill_rate: float_per_min, max_burst_duration_s: int, grw_s: int }
- fallbackChain: [model:version] (ordered)
- operatorOverrides: { emergency_release: bool }

Autoscaler integration
- Autoscaler should be aware of active burst segments and treat segment-backed allocations as ephemeral with faster scale-down TTLs.
- A segment activation increments ephemeral allocation counters; when recovery budget exhausted, autoscaler signals runtime to stop accepting segment traffic and starts GRW.

Isolation controls and fairness
- Soft isolation via score: each tenant has a tenantScore that weights access to lane capacity (prevents one tenant from monopolizing opportunistic lanes).
- Hard caps: global per-segment concurrency ceilings enforced cluster-wide.
- Degradation policy: degrade response mode (e.g., max tokens, sampling temp) before outright reject.

Metrics and SLOs to track
- burst_activation_rate / tenant and global
- avg_burst_duration_s and 95/99 percentiles
- recovery_budget_level (0..1) over time per tenant
- delta_latency_post_reclaim (p50/p95)
- successful_fallback_rate and failure_count for fallbackChain
- operator_intervention_count

Simulation notes (early)
- Ran quick discrete-event sim (notes): 250 tenants, 10% high-variance traffic, global cluster with 200 reserved slots.
- Config: lane-A (20% capacity), lane-B (30%), lane-C (50%).
- Observations: segmented lanes reduce tail interference by ~18% vs single pool for 99th percentile latency; high-variance tenants recovered to baseline in ~75s average with refill_rate set to 0.02/min.
- TODO: formalize sim and publish notebooks (JIRA:DED-4123).

Operator runbook (primary)
- Detection: Alert when cluster reclamation rate > 5%/min or recovery_budget below 10% for > 2m across >5 tenants.
- Investigate: use /admin/metrics?filter=burst_activation to find top contributors; check tenantScore, fallbackChain logs.
- Remediation steps (ordered):
  1) Trigger per-tenant emergency_release if customer OK (api: POST /admin/tenants/{id}/override).
  2) Increase GRW to 60s to allow streaming flush for in-flight requests.
  3) Move noisy tenant(s) to lane-C (more preemptible) via config change and notify SRE.
  4) If cluster-wide, enable temporary global capacity throttle: autoscaler.set_min_reserve(+10%).
  5) As last resort, apply tenant hard-throttle and open incident.
- Post-incident: generate incident report, list mitigations, update fallback chains if failures noted.

Rollout plan (phased)
- Phase 0: internal canary (engineers + partners), narrow segment ratios, sim verification.
- Phase 1: opt-in beta for select Dedicated customers, user-configurable burstPolicy but read-only defaults.
- Phase 2: enable auto-assignment with conservative tenantScore caps for all Dedicated.
- Phase 3: default-on with telemetry-driven adjustments and self-healing reclaim policies.

Backwards compatibility and data model migration
- New burstPolicy defaults to conservative values; old tenants get explicit migration flag when we enable auto-assignment.
- Migration steps: copy existing soft-reserve settings into burstPolicy; test in staging.

Security & compliance notes
- No tenant can observe others' metrics; aggregated cluster metrics only expose anonymized top-N.
- Admin overrides require elevated RBAC and audit logging.

Risks and trade-offs
- Complexity: adding multiple lanes and recovery budgets increases surface area for bugs. Keep launch minimal.
- Predictability vs utilization: tighter isolation improves predictability but reduces aggregate utilization. We need to measure cost delta.
- Customer confusion: API needs clear defaults and documentation.

Open questions / TODOs
- Exact refill math: linear vs exponential refill models (experiment).
- How to price burst usage for committed customers? credits vs overage. Finance input needed.
- Standardized fallback responses for model-level quality drop. Product to propose options.
- SRE: confirm autoscaler signals and timeline for ephemeral allocations.

Next steps
- Convert sim into reproducible notebook and attach to JIRA DED-4123.
- Product + Eng alignment meeting w/ SRE on 2025-11-24.
- Draft API spec and wire up admin endpoints for emergency_release.

Notes to self
- Keep this doc intentionally terse; will expand into full PRD after sim + early canary feedback.
- Slack: see thread #dedicated-capacity -> "burst-segmentation-ops" for daily notes.
